title: RTBF Sweeper: verifiable timestamps & deletion manifests
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Customers in regulated geographies and enterprise accounts require provable right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) workflows that can demonstrate when PII was removed and from which storage tiers. Current deletion paths are partially manual (ad hoc purge jobs, ad-hoc SQL deletes for legacy tables) and lack a tamper-evident artifact that can be attached to customer deletion receipts.

Goal: Build a deterministic 'sweeper' pipeline that executes scheduled and on-demand RTBF purges across storage surfaces (S3 object prefixes, DB rows, index shards, KV caches) and emits an auditable, time-stamped deletion manifest bundle for each request. The manifest should include residency metadata (region, tenant), the set of logical resources touched, token counts removed (approx), and a verifiable monotonic event id and signature to support downstream attestation and retention reporting.

Scope: This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and integration points (Console UI receipts, backend purge runner, evidence export). Implementation tasks will be split to ENG for runner & attestations and DESIGN for the Console receipt UX.

Out of scope: Replacing encryption/KMS; full legal text for customer-facing deletion certificates (will surface templates for legal to approve), or live migration of archived cold stores (handled by separate migration project).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled and on-demand RTBF sweeper can target tenant-scoped data across S3 prefixes, primary Postgres rows, and Redis KV namespaces via a single control-plane API

Each purge run produces a deletion manifest bundle containing: run_id (monotonic), timestamp (ISO8601), region, tenant_id, list of touched logical resource identifiers, counts (estimated tokens/objects), and a checksum of the bundle
Deletion manifests are stored immutably for 365 days in the evidence bucket and are retrievable via the Console and API with proper RBAC
Console exposes 'Request deletion evidence' action returning a signed manifest and human-readable summary within 5 minutes of a completed purge
Automated verification job runs nightly and raises an alert when any manifest references a resource that still contains data according to a lightweight scanner (false-positive rate < 3%)
All code paths touch existing audit logging and produce linked GitHub PR and Confluence runbook references for post-mortem
Security review completed and threat model updated; any KMS/HSM interactions documented
Documentation (PRD + runbook) published and linked from Console help center
tasks: Define manifest schema and signing format (product + security)
Design Console receipt UX and API surface for evidence retrieval
Implement purge runner orchestration with region-aware resource adapters
Implement immutable evidence storage lifecycle (365d retention + archive policy)
Add nightly verification scanner and alerting rules
Add E2E test harness + load test to simulate 10k tenant sweeps/month
Prepare customer-facing deletion certificate template for legal review
updates: 2025-03-02: Ticket created by Priya Nair. Kickoff meeting scheduled; initial tech spike requested (ENG).

2025-03-04: Spike findings (ENG-2389) show Postgres row-level deletes can be batched with seq scan window; S3 deletes require eventual consistency handling. Decided to emit object-level keys in manifest but rely on object checksum rather than content fingerprint to limit scan cost.

2025-03-06: Design sketch completed - Console will surface a one-click 'Export deletion manifest' and show a shortened summary (resources touched, size estimate). Anita Shah (Design) provided initial mockups.
2025-03-08: Security workshop: use KMS for manifest envelope signing; HSM optional for enterprise installs. Agreed to add signing key rotation policy to runbook.
2025-03-10: Engineering landed initial PR for control-plane API schema (PR #4123). Integration tests pending. Assignee requested additional time for verification scanner thresholds.
2025-03-10: PM updated acceptance criteria to cap nightly scanner false-positive rate and set retrieval SLA (5 minutes).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large tenants may produce huge manifests making retrieval and storage expensive. Mitigation: manifest summarizes logical resources and provides paginated detail links to archived chunks; set chunking policy by size.
Risk: S3 eventual consistency could cause scanner false positives. Mitigation: scanner tolerates 2-hour carve-out window and re-checks before alerting.
Risk: Malicious tenant could repeatedly request deletions to create storage churn. Mitigation: rate-limit on-demand RTBF requests and billing signals to customer success for pattern detection.
release_notes: Feature: RTBF sweeper with signed deletion manifests and Console evidence export
Admin: New RBAC privilege `evidence.view` required to retrieve manifests
Operational: Nightly verification scanner and new alerts in PagerDuty service 'privacy-sweeper'
